A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AgriPath benchmark and architectural comparison. Their main text, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix material.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification experiments, cross-domain evaluations, hyperparameter sweeps and failure analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 reports original model evaluations, including additional ConvNeXt-Tiny experiments and a new class-level domain-composition analysis.

M1.justification: The retained methods use the same CNN fine-tuning, contrastive linear probing, LoRA and frozen-vision adaptation, prompting formats and output parsing. ConvNeXt-Tiny is an additional evaluated baseline, rather than a new proposed algorithm or adaptation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same source datasets, 16 crops, 41 diseases, 65 crop–disease classes and laboratory/field classification task. Duplicate correction and class-group filtering concern data handling and analysis within this coverage, not new tasks or domains.

E2.justification: V3 adds ConvNeXt-Tiny throughout the combined, lab-only and field-only comparisons, with corresponding appendix sweeps. This substantially strengthens the CNN reference previously represented only by ResNet-50, adding a comparator that leads the combined evaluation. All previous comparators remain.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 newly reports remedying hash-detected cross-split overlap affecting less than 6.5% of instances, a consequential correction to evaluation independence. New Section 4.5 introduces class-size controls and a minimum of 11 field test samples, retaining 12 balanced and eight lab-dominant classes. The PDFs do not establish precisely how cleanup affected splits or which models were retrained.

E4.justification: New Section 4.5 tests whether architectural differences persist after controlling class size and separating balanced from lab-dominant training composition. This adds substantial evidence about a confound in the existing robustness comparison. Appendix B adds a parameter-efficiency comparison, while the generative failure analysis is reorganized and loses its quantitative hallucination breakdown.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. V3's minimum field-support threshold is an evaluation sample-selection rule, not a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V3 adds ConvNeXt-Tiny results, including the leading 92.9 macro-F1 in Table 1, and new domain-composition findings. Retained scores also change: full-training ResNet-50 field F1 changes from 70.3 to 69.9, and Qwen2.5-VL-7B zero-shot MCQ F1 from 65.9 to 66.9. These are revised reports alongside reported data cleanup, not established same-setting gains. V3 removes the 431 parse-failure count and 12.69% hallucination fraction while retaining 39.7% empty outputs.

T1.justification: No formal assumptions, proofs, theorems or substantive mathematical derivations are added or revised. Expanded PSR wording explains an existing metric rather than introducing new mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract broadens the claim that CNNs achieve the highest accuracy from lab imagery to in-domain imagery. The principal contributions remain the domain-aware benchmark, three-paradigm comparison and deployment-dependent model-selection argument.

C2.justification: V3 adds a substantive account of domain composition controlling generalization and qualifies class-level field evaluation by available support. Section 4.4 reverses the stated generative transfer asymmetry and replaces its web-pretraining explanation with an explanation based on field training tolerating laboratory conditions. Section 5.1 adds residual near-duplicate risk and explains how domain imbalance limits class estimates and aggregate interpretation.

D1.justification: V3 replaces the anonymous dataset placeholder with a specific dataset URL and documents ontology mapping, source-based domain labels, class-stratified splitting, image hashing and total/trainable parameter counts. These are mostly additional disclosures. Conversely, it omits v1's explanation that MCQ choices contain the true label and three randomly selected alternatives. Existing framework, LoRA, inference and parsing details remain.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, reference list and positioning relative to agricultural datasets and VLM research are unchanged. ConvNeXt-Tiny is added experimentally without an accompanying expansion of cited research.

P1.justification: V3 renames Section 3 to Methodology, revises selected methodological, results and limitations paragraphs, and inserts the new analysis and efficiency appendix. Existing appendices are renumbered and the CNN appendix is organized by architecture. The overall narrative and substantial portions of the text remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds a parameter-count table and three ConvNeXt-Tiny sweep tables, extends and reorders comparison rows, and labels Table 1's metrics explicitly as macro averages. Figures 3–4 are recomposed; Figure 4 substitutes a different potato photograph while retaining identical prediction values. The distribution plot and both confusion-matrix graphics remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The additional CNN comparator, domain-composition analysis and concrete dataset access information make v3's comparison better supported and more usable. Reported duplicate cleanup also addresses an important validity concern, although its implementation and connection to revised results remain insufficiently documented. These gains outweigh limited reporting losses, particularly the removed failure statistics and Figure 4's unexplained photograph replacement with unchanged predictions, but do not establish a major improvement.
